chain.label: Dispatch into freezing drizzle conditions
chain.trigger: the flight release ... indicated that IFR conditions with light freezing drizzle and mist were reported at LBB and forecast to continue beyond the flight's estimated time of arrival

chain.label: Captain fatigued from night-shift schedule and cumulative sleep debt
chain.trigger: fatigue due to the time of day in which the accident occurred and a cumulative sleep debt, which likely impaired the captain's performance

chain.label: Airplane accumulated airframe ice descending into LBB in freezing drizzle
chain.trigger: the airplane began to accumulate ice again when it descended into moderate icing conditions resulting from light freezing drizzle, a weather condition ... outside its icing certification envelope

caused_by.evidence: dispatched ... into freezing drizzle conditions ... outside the ATR 42's certification icing envelope

chain.label: Flap asymmetry on approach (left flap partial extension, right flap no extension)
chain.trigger: a flap asymmetry had occurred in which the right flaps did not extend and the left flaps extended partially (8° to 10°)

caused_by.evidence: the investigation could not rule out the possibility that ice could have formed and either delayed or restricted the flap extension and resulted in a flap asymmetry

chain.label: Captain failed to communicate his troubleshooting plan; poor CRM
chain.trigger: the captain did not communicate to the first officer his intentions for managing the situation

chain.label: Captain did not follow QRH flap-anomaly/go-around procedure; troubleshot circuit breakers instead
chain.trigger: the captain retrieved and used a flashlight to check the circuit breakers ... no reference was made to the QRH

caused_by.evidence: you know what? we have no flaps
the captain pursued his own plan of action without providing any guidance to the first officer

chain.label: Flight crew failed to monitor and maintain airspeed during the approach
chain.trigger: the airplane's airspeed decreased from about 155 kts to 125 kts ... neither flight crewmember made any verbal reference about airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the first officer's failure to maintain airspeed ... likely resulted from being distracted by the flap anomaly, the captain's actions in response to it

chain.label: Captain decided to continue the unstabilized approach rather than go around
chain.trigger: the first officer asked, 'should I go around,' and the captain replied, 'no,' and then stated, 'keep descending'

caused_by.evidence: the captain made a judgment call not to go around because things started piling up, and it was better to land than to go around
fatigue likely degraded the captain's performance

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall developed at low altitude as airspeed decayed below minimum safe speed
chain.trigger: the aural stall warning and the stick shaker activated for the third time ... the airspeed ... was about 124 kts, approximately 19 kts below the minimum safe airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's failure to monitor and maintain a minimum safe airspeed ... resulted in an aerodynamic stall at low altitude

chain.label: Uncommanded roll and pitch/yaw oscillations following the stall
chain.trigger: the airplane experienced an uncommanded roll followed by a series of roll, yaw, and pitch oscillations, which continued until ground impact

caused_by.evidence: about 2 seconds after the stall warning occurred, the airplane experienced an uncommanded roll
the captain's failure to immediately respond to the aural stall warning, the stick shaker, and the TAWS warning resulted in his inability to arrest the airplane's descent

chain.label: Airplane crashed short of the runway
chain.trigger: the CVR captured the sound of impact

caused_by.evidence: impacted the ground ... and slid for a distance

chain.label: Captain sustained serious injuries; first officer sustained minor injuries
chain.trigger: The captain sustained serious injuries, and the first officer sustained minor injuries
